issues.evidence: All recorded facts match the sources and the claim would otherwise qualify (reported 2026-10-14, 2 days after the 2026-10-12 incident, within the 5-day deadline of contract Article 4.1; no Article 3 exclusion; C2 collision damage is in the Policy Schedule; all C2-required documents provided per Article 4.3; not-at-fault waiver of Article 5.2 gives €0 deductible since the policyholder is not at fault and the third party is identified; €1,200 is below the €1,500 assessor threshold of Article 6.1 and below the €14,000 market value). HOWEVER, the handler playbook states: 'When the other driver is a commercial vehicle (van, truck, lorry, delivery vehicle), refer the claim to a handler so Veridia can recover the money from their insurer.' The accident report shows Vehicle B is a Ford Transit Custom with VEHICLE TYPE 'Van' belonging to Rapid Livraisons SARL (a delivery company), i.e. a commercial/delivery van, so this playbook rule is triggered by the documents and the claim must be referred to a handler, not paid automatically. The staged automatic payout of €1,200 with 'assessor required: no' therefore must not be approved as an automatic payment.

verdict.summary: Every recorded fact matches the email, the signed accident report and the repair quote, and the claim is in time, covered under C2, fully documented and exclusion-free — but because the other vehicle is a commercial delivery van (Ford Transit Custom of Rapid Livraisons SARL), the playbook requires referral to a handler for recovery from the third party's insurer, so the automatic €1,200 payment must not be approved.
